name: Chandivali Studio
description: Chandivali “Studio,” As It Is Known, Began Its Journey In 1940 When Chandrarao Kadam Purchased A Large Parcel Of Land At Chandivali, Near Powai Lake In Mumbai, India. His Idea Was To Create Multiple And Diverse Filming Locations In One Place, Use Them For Shooting His Own Films But Also Make These Locations Available To Other Film Producers. This Innovative Concept Was Unprecedented In The Indian Movie Industry And Became A Template That Many Others Would Follow. It Took Mr. Kadam Nearly Four Years To Clear And Level The Existing Forestland And A Lifetime To Create And Develop The Parcel’s Various Themed Areas. Chandivali Outdoor Location Opened For Business In 1944.

From grand soundstages to cutting-edge post-production facilities, film studios play a vital role in shaping the magic of cinema. Whether producing large-scale blockbusters or intimate indie films, these studios provide the foundation for storytelling at its finest, blending artistry with technical brilliance.

Yash Raj Films: A Legacy of Excellence in Indian Cinema

Yash Raj Films (YRF) stands as a pillar of Indian cinema, synonymous with grandeur, romance, and timeless storytelling. Founded by the visionary Yash Chopra, YRF has redefined Bollywood with its unparalleled craftsmanship, producing films that resonate across generations. From heartwarming love stories to gripping thrillers, the studio has consistently set new benchmarks in filmmaking. Beyond its artistic brilliance, YRF has also built an empire with its state-of-the-art studios, fostering talent and innovation. With its keen eye for storytelling and commitment to excellence, Yash Raj Films continues to shape the future of Indian cinema, leaving an indelible mark on audiences worldwide.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve been attending Aerial Yoga classes at The Square Powai, and while the classes themselves are enjoyable, I’ve found some of the policies to be frustrating and unfair. One of the biggest issues is that the studio has strict policies regarding missed classes, but these are not clearly communicated when signing up.

For instance, Tara can cancel classes last minute, which is understandable, but if members inform the studio in advance about planned leaves or personal situations, these are still considered as missed classes. Even medical emergencies don’t seem to be taken into account, which feels unreasonable.

The lack of transparency about these policies upfront is disappointing. Had I known about them, I would have considered whether to sign up in the first place. Clear communication from the beginning would have been much appreciated. It’s important for studios to be upfront about policies, especially when they could impact members' experience.

I hope the management can review these policies and how they are communicated to new members to avoid any future misunderstandings.

featured_reviews.name: Arpit Porwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bollywood Park is a decent place to visit, but not as grand as expected. Most of the film sets are either covered or not accessible, so you only get a glimpse of a few memorable spots like Taarak Mehta ka Ooltah Chasmah sets from far that are ok for quick photos.

The museum section is actually nice for clicking pictures, with well-designed setups and film-themed decor. The live show was the highlight well performed and quite engaging. Overall, it’s good for a one-time visit, especially if you enjoy Bollywood vibes, but don’t go in expecting full studio-style access as ticket price does not justify it.

featured_reviews.name: Mesh
featured_reviews.review_text:
HIGHLIGHT - If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

My recent visit to Mumbai Film City was far from what I had hoped. To start, the nearest metro station is Aarey, it is about 4 km away. From there, take an auto (no more than ₹150) straight to the official ticket counter. Be cautious, several individuals may try to sell you tickets along the way at inflated prices. Avoid them, as they are scammers.

After a long wait, we were taken inside the premises by an AC bus. Unfortunately, the experience was underwhelming from the beginning. Compared to Hyderabad's Film City, this one feels small, restricted, and poorly organized. Most of what you see are large tin sheets covering the sets, there is no access to the actual sets themselves. It felt like being shown billboards of what you could see, but never actually do.

The tour ends at Bollywood Park, which hosts a few staged performances. This was the only mildly enjoyable part. The on site restaurant is strictly vegetarian, which may not appeal to everyone, and the food was overpriced for its quality.

Overall, Mumbai Film City lacks substance, feels commercialized, and fails to deliver the behind the scenes magic one would expect. If you have been to Hyderabad's version, you will likely find this visit a complete letdown.

featured_reviews.name: Vijay Desai
featured_reviews.review_text: First off, the location of this place on Google maps is wrong. It is inside the Film city, not outside. This is just the ticket office and where the bus picks you up. We were late but they were nice to call us and then wait for us. There were two half empty buses but no indication which one we should board. We boarded one only to find out later that it was the Hindi bus. So we asked for the buses to be stopped so we can transfer to the bus with English speaking guide. We spent in hour in the bus touring the Film city with only 2 stops. One was the famous temple that is reused in movies by changing Gods. They were getting it ready for a Shiva temple. That was interesting. Everything else was just drive by. Then they brought us to the "theme park" which had some interesting props and some shooting going on that we could watch. We saw Kadar Khan and few other actors. Then there was a very long (1-1/2 hr) live show which included dances by a SRK double. But we were basically made to watch rest of the mediocre show because the buses won't come to get you until the show is over. No one could ever tell us how long some activity is going to take which would have helped set expectations. The first 1 hour of actual tour is fun. Maybe 30 min in the theme park is sufficient. But rest of the 1-1/2 hrs of the talent show is just torture! Hardly anything was in English so we had to keep translating for our daughter who doesn't speak Hindi and also for several non Indians. All in all, kind of OK but could be better and more entertaining.
